lines.en: I pace along the base of the wall.
Bow on my back, my stride is steady.
I climb the ladder to the tower.
I tramp across the muddy camp.
I fall back to a fresh firing spot.
I skirt the palisade to the battlement.
I count the paces to range my shot.
My boots crunch on the gravel path.
I move to another stretch of wall.
I slip sideways through the alley.
I stride on with a full quiver.
I walk on, eyes on the distance.
Arrow nocked, I hold ready.
My eyes sweep beyond the wall.
I test the draw of my bow.
I lean on the battlement a while.
I count the arrows I have left.
My fingers trace the bow's grain.
The wind stirs my hood.
Shoulders tight, I await orders.
I tilt my bow against the glare.
No slacking on watch.
I raise a hand for you to halt.
My bow's tip swings toward you.
I squint to judge your range.
Friend, or a raider?
My eyes are on your hands.
Halt and give your name.

lines.zh: 看清楚了，这一箭不落空。
lines.en: Look closely; this arrow will not miss.
You have stepped into my arc.
I tilt my head at your accent.
No wandering under my gate.
I hold the bow low and wait.
My gaze runs from boots to crown.
I nearly drop my bow.
I grit my teeth and stay quiet.
My armour took most of it.
I drop to one knee and push up.
My arm will not rise.
An arrowhead split my sleeve.
Blood seeps into my glove.
I lean on the wall and pant.
The rim of my hood is sheared off.
I must fall back and reposition.
Good arrows? Let me see.
My eyes fix on your quiver.
A fresh string smells fine.
That string beats mine.
I reach out to take it.
Honed arrowheads gleam.
Have you brought any drink?
I swallow hard.
Will you trade for half my quiver?
I lean in to study your gear.
You jarred my arrows loose.
Mind the bow, the string slips.
I step aside from the battlement.
My shoulder smarts from the knock.
It is crowded here, back up.
I steady my quiver and hold post.
The bump slides my hood down.
I wave you back from crowding.
I nearly lose my footing.
Two sentries should not collide.
I give her my finest arrow.
We hold the battlement side by side.
She straightens my bowstring.
I shoulder her quiver for her.
We whisper between watches.
Her aim is truer than mine.
We linger when the watch changes.
Two bows lean together on the wall.
I have learned her range by heart.

lines.zh: 她的手套磨得和我一样
lines.en: Her gloves are worn just like mine.
I pick up a fallen arrow.
I wipe the nock clean and stow it.
I gather up a broken shaft.
I retrieve an arrow that missed.
I slot the arrow back in my belt.
I pick up a whetstone.
I collect the scattered fletching.
I take an arrow the enemy dropped.
I stoop and pick up a bowstring.
I return an arrow someone dropped.
A shadow moves beyond the wall.
I lift the bow's aim.
The foe is in range.
I crouch low for cover.
The target breaks from the trees.
I seat the nock on the string.
Wind is left; I will adjust.
I have spotted their banner.
Footsteps near the camp.
I aim first, then shout warning.
It is close enough; no rush.
I draw the string back an inch.
That one is heading for the gate.
My eyes track it steadily.
I track its motion with the bow.
I slow my breath before loosing.
I work out the lead.
It goes left; I wait for right.
I hold my aim on its chest.
Full draw; do not waver.
Ten more paces and I loose.
It ducks behind the wall; I shift.
I keep watching that gap.
The wind turned; I adjust.
It hesitates; I stay still.
My fingers begin to ache.
The moment it shows, I shoot.

lines.zh: 弓弦绷紧，我等你走出掩体。
lines.en: Bowstring taut, I wait for you to leave cover.
At this range I am sure.
The bow's limbs feel like iron.
I wait for it to turn.
The arrow flies straight and true.
I release; the string hums.
An arrow pins its shoulder.
It charges; I shoot while backing.
A second arrow follows the first.
I aimed for its eye.
Close in, I block with my bow.
My bow's tip cracks its face.
Sweat covers my drawing hand.
One more arrow to be certain.
It staggers, arrow in its side.
I loose three arrows without pause.
The shaft grazes its ear.
This arrow takes its knee.
My arrow pierces its raised shield.
The last arrow puts it down.
I give ground, still loosing shots.
The string cuts into my fingers.
I step out of the tower's shadow.
Quiver hung, I take my post.
The camp gains an archer.
I sling the bow across my back.
A new sentry on the wall.
First I check the wind.
My boots take the stone stair.
I slip out from behind the gate.
Bow in hand, I stand at the merlon.
This stretch is mine to hold.
I pluck the empty string once.
I settle in and scan around.
Fire is eating my quiver.
I fell from the wall.
Water pours into my armour.
The blast throws up a spray of brick.
Their arrow found me too.
Spellfire burns through my leather.
Too hungry to draw the bow.
Lightning splits my bow.
The wall beneath me is gone.
